speaker: client
text: For VBUS, +5V, and BAT-, some power stub traces measure 0.4–1.2 mm even though the requirements document specifies ≥2 mm. Since the inner-layer copper pours carry the bulk current, I think this is electrically acceptable, but was it intentional rather than a missed rule?

speaker: client
text: For VBUS and BAT−, which see the worst-case simultaneous current of up to ~3.2 A from 2.4 A charging plus ~0.8 A system load, I need confirmation on two points. First, do the F.Cu and In2.Cu pours remain contiguous from the USB-C or battery connector through to the AXP2101 VBUS and BAT pins, without any thin trace in series? Second, are there enough stitching vias between F.Cu and In2.Cu on those nets—typically 6+ vias for ~3.2 A? If both conditions are met, I am happy with the design. What concerns me is any 0.4 mm series bottleneck, since a 0.4 mm outer-layer trace carrying 3 A would run hot, with about a ~60 °C rise over ambient.
